credited_works: Georgius Pachymeres, Paraphrasis in omnia opera Dionysii Areopagitae (NEW, 71-568, interwoven)
conclusive_evidence_this_pass: data/pd_research/cgpg_split_proposals.json PG003: every work range interleaves Pseudo-Dionysius' text with Georgius Pachymeres' paraphrase chapter by chapter, plus embedded quotations (e.g. Gregory of Nazianzus' hymn at locus 310); word counts of the ranges are roughly double the TLG word counts for this reason.

The proposals' consistency review: the Pachymeres entry (71-568) fully overlaps all five Dionysius works and is self-flagged 'interwoven, not separable by column range; a splitter must treat it as an annotation, not a carve'.

The five Dionysius column ranges themselves verify (boundaries pinned by verbatim explicit+incipit pairs at 192/193, 299/300, 505/506, 539/540), but carving them would serve each Dionysius work with the Pachymeres paraphrase silently embedded, roughly doubling every work and mis-attributing the paraphrase text.
why_not_resolved: Not a passage-level problem and not impossible by column carve. Migne prints a display head at every switch, and 4 of them survive in our OCR (plus 7 chapter heads) (measured by scripts/measure_pg003_blocks.py, listed in data/pg003_blocks.json). Every one of them OPENS its row rather than sitting mid-row, so the switches fall on locus boundaries and a locus carve can express them; intra-row segmentation is not what this needs. What blocks the carve is coverage, not granularity: most of the volume's 459 rows sit inside a run whose opening head the OCR dropped, and a boundary we cannot see is exactly the one that would file a block under the wrong author. Recovering the dropped heads needs the PG 3 page images.
recommendation: read the heads off the page images, then carve on loci like any other volume. The surviving heads in data/pg003_blocks.json give the shape to check that recovery against.
precedent: same flag pattern as data/corpus_changes/aelius_dionysius_schwabe.reocr-flag.json (interleaved series a range carve cannot separate)

superseded.was: A column-range carve cannot separate the two authors: each served row alternates Dionysius text and Pachymeres paraphrase at the passage level. Serving the ranges as the Dionysius works would embed a second author's text under the wrong urn; serving the whole volume as Pachymeres would mis-attribute Dionysius. The separation needs passage-level (intra-row) segmentation.
superseded.wrong_because: the bytes do not show a passage-level alternation, and the display heads reported absent are present, garbled. Migne marks each switch with a printed head; the OCR read the Latin ones as Greek letter shapes (PARAPHRASIS PACHYMERAE -> ΡΑΗΑΡΗΚΑΘ ΡΑΩΙΥΜΕΛ at locus 151), which is why a Greek search found none and the interleave was taken to be unmarked.
